title: ADMM-Net: A Deep Learning Approach for Compressive Sensing MRI

citations.claim: Yang et al. proposed ADMM-Net, a deep architecture derived from unrolling the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) algorithm for compressive sensing MRI reconstruction.
ADMM-Net maps each iteration of the ADMM algorithm to a stage in a data flow graph, with three types of operations per stage: reconstruction, denoising (shrinkage), and multiplier update.

In ADMM-Net, all parameters including image transforms, shrinkage functions, penalty parameters, and update rates are discriminatively trained end-to-end from data using L-BFGS optimization and back-propagation.

ADMM-Net replaces the hand-crafted shrinkage function (e.g., soft or hard thresholding) with a learnable piecewise linear function parameterized by a set of control points, enabling the network to learn more general nonlinear transforms from data.

Yang et al. proposed two variants: Basic-ADMM-Net, which introduces auxiliary variables in the transform domain, and Generic-ADMM-Net, which introduces the auxiliary variable in the image domain and uses gradient-descent sub-iterations within each stage.
ADMM-Net does not constrain the convolution filters in the reconstruction layer and the convolution layer to be identical, thereby increasing the network capacity beyond the original ADMM algorithm.

ADMM-Net parameters can be initialized from a model-based CS-MRI baseline (e.g., DCT basis with l1 regularization and soft thresholding), making the initialized network an exact realization of the ADMM optimization process.
ADMM-Net achieved state-of-the-art MR image reconstruction accuracy while being approximately 10 to 13 times faster than competing iterative methods such as BM3D-MRI and PANO.

Yang et al. demonstrated that adding more stages (corresponding to more ADMM iterations) is more effective than adding more sub-iterations within each stage for improving reconstruction quality in ADMM-Net.

ADMM-Net is an early and influential example of algorithm unrolling, where a classical iterative optimization algorithm is mapped to a deep network whose parameters are learned from data rather than hand-tuned.

The ADMM-Net framework naturally combines the merits of model-based approaches, which incorporate domain knowledge via the optimization structure, with deep learning approaches that learn parameters from data.

Yang et al. formulated the general CS-MRI reconstruction as minimizing a data fidelity term plus multiple regularization terms in transform domains, solved via ADMM by splitting into reconstruction, shrinkage, and multiplier update subproblems.

ADMM-Net demonstrated that a learned network trained from brain MR data generalized competitively to chest MR data, suggesting that learned local transforms and nonlinear functions transfer across imaging domains.

do_not_claim: ADMM-Net was applied to chromatogram baseline correction or 1-D signal processing
ADMM-Net uses ISTA or proximal gradient descent as its base algorithm
ADMM-Net was the first algorithm unrolling paper (LISTA by Gregor and LeCun 2010 preceded it)
ADMM-Net uses ReLU activations (it uses learned piecewise linear functions)
